text: /// Ask the user about each undecided offer, then record the answers.
/// hook dispatch and anything an agent triggers use a quiet or capturing
/// output, so they return here immediately without touching stdin. In those
/// contexts the candidates surface as a `SessionStart` hint instead (see
/// Only explicit answers are recorded — the default ("ask me later") leaves
/// the dependency undecided, so reflexively hitting Enter never permanently
/// declines anything, and Escape leaves the remaining offers undecided too.
Some(_) => {}  // ask me later — record nothing
None => break, // Esc — leave the rest undecided
/// A short human summary of what a discovered plugin contributes, shown in
/// the consent prompt. Emphasizes the facets that matter to a
/// trust decision — a plugin that only ships skills is lower-stakes than one
/// that runs a hook or an MCP server.
fn count_phrase(n: usize, singular: &str, plural: &str) -> Option<String> {
(n > 0).then(|| format!("{n} {}", if n == 1 { singular } else { plural }))

rationale:
`discover` sets each offer's `description` to `describe_plugin(&plugin.manifest)`, which joins `count_phrase` outputs for skill groups (`manifest.skills`), hooks, MCP servers and subcommands, omitting zero counts and pluralizing correctly (`count_phrase`), falling back to "agent extensions" when all are zero. `prompt_for_consent` shows it in the question: "Dependency `<name>` provides <what>. Enable it?".

Untested: `describe_plugin`/`count_phrase` are private with no unit test, and the prompt needs a TTY; judged from code. Note: for a crate plugin, validation appends the default `skills/` group, so the skill-group count includes it; the facets named are still accurate kinds.
requirement: An interactive consent prompt SHOULD say which kinds of extension the plugin contributes: skill groups, hooks, MCP servers, subcommands.
